decision: Chose figure-it-out as the playbook, not the narrow Refactoring playbook
why: the change touches four handlers, the boot walk, two wire protocols and the shell client, so it is cross-cutting rather than one focused reshape

decision: Definition of done is one registration per kind reached by every verb
why: a predicate that can be tested, not a feeling: register a stub third kind and assert every verb dispatches to it without touching the handlers

decision: Confirmed the registry cannot live in ores.synthetic.api
why: that component cannot see the ores.synthetic.core repositories the per-kind row loading needs, so the seam must be supplied from the service layer

decision: Named the existing integration suites as the behaviour pin
why: they drive the real handlers over real NATS and a real database, so they catch behaviour the unit tests cannot

decision: Rebuilt the dev database from current SQL before pinning
why: the freshly built test binary refused to start: its schema fingerprint e4803181e989327c did not match the database's ed8466d86118a2ce, because main's SQL moved after the last rebuild

decision: Baseline pin captured on the unmodified tree
why: the two integration suites are the behaviour contract for the whole change, so they must be green before anything moves

decision: Ran an arena over the registry shape instead of picking one myself
why: the seam is a one-way door: every future asset class registers through it, and the layering rule forces a non-obvious placement

decision: Found that the vote-changing constraint is a repo convention, not taste
why: polymorphic_types_over_nats.org mandates one NATS subject per concrete type, so merging the two simulate payloads into one variant request is disallowed

decision: Recorded the before measurement for the reader-load delta
why: the claim that this change lowers reader load needs a number taken before the change, on the same tree
evidence: wc -l: 1883 lines across the 6 handler files; grep predicate: 55 hits

decision: Synthesis: base candidate 3, graft the startable() gate, keep the factory and the two simulate subjects
why: candidate 3 is the only candidate that honours both repo conventions; the graft is the smallest fix for the Goal's enable-exists-once clause

decision: Cross-judge confirmed candidate 3 (25 vs 19) on repo conventions
why: candidate 2 merged the two simulate subjects into one variant request, which the project's NATS convention forbids; candidate 3 unifies only the server-side envelope

decision: Enlarged the graft after the judge: make_feed() owns gate, child loading and construction
why: the Goal says enable and child loading exist once, and candidate 3 still wrote that sequence in three files; moving only the predicate was too small

decision: Caught that candidate 3 breaks preview_shape by moving its process helper
why: the judge read the kept verb and found it calls make_preview_process, so the helper must move to a shared header instead of into the IR registration
